---
title: "Exercise · Portability"
---

A short, guided task. Complete it before moving on to the lab.

## Task

For the Pico you have been modeling across Part 3, write the beginning of a
**portable Pico definition** that keeps the Open Engineering identity
separate from the runtime identity:

```yaml
# portable-pico.yaml
oepid: oep.pico.alice.v1
identity:
  type: did
  public:
    method: webvh
    url: https://engine-a.example.com/picos/alice/did.json
relationships:
  identity:
    method: peer
messaging:
  protocol: didcomm
authorization:
  mechanism: channel-policy
```

Answer the questions below.

::: {.callout-note}
This example follows the shape from the [lesson](index.qmd). The important
point is that identity should become a first-class property of a Pico rather
than an implementation-specific extension.
:::

## Success criteria

- [ ] Your definition keeps the Open Engineering identifier (`oepid`)
      separate from the runtime `did:webvh`.
- [ ] You separate identity, relationships, messaging, and authorization
      into distinct sections.
- [ ] You can name at least **two** of the four remaining-work areas that
      stand between this definition and a fully portable Pico.

## Automatable check

Validate your definition parses:

```bash
pico parse portable-pico.yaml --out /tmp/pp.json \
  && echo "OK: portable Pico definition parses"
```

The command exits `0` and prints the `OK:` line when well-formed.

## Reflect

- Why must the Open Engineering identifier and the runtime DID remain
  distinct?
- What would "losing a cryptographic key should not mean losing the Pico"
  require of an implementation?
